## Facts and statements

- [statement] NINDS describes dopamine produced by substantia nigra neurons as a chemical messenger supporting smooth, purposeful movements. (low confidence) — https://www.ninds.nih.gov/health-information/disorders/parkinsons-disease · keywords: Basal ganglia circuitry and dopamine neurobiology
- [statement] The nigrostriatal axonal projection carries the influence of substantia nigra pars compacta dopaminergic neurons to the striatum, as described by the axonal review and the circuit review. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-13) — https://www.dovepress.com/degeneration-of-nigrostriatal-dopaminergic-axons-in-parkinsons-disease-peer-reviewed-fulltext-article-NDT · keywords: Basal ganglia circuitry and dopamine neurobiology · also: https://journals.physiology.org/doi/full/10.1152/jn.00527.2025
- [statement] Rocha and colleagues describe the striatum as the main input hub within the interconnected basal ganglia nuclei. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-05-07) — https://journals.physiology.org/doi/full/10.1152/jn.00527.2025 · keywords: Basal ganglia circuitry and dopamine neurobiology
- [statement] Rocha and colleagues describe direct-pathway spiny projection neurons as GABAergic neurons expressing Drd1 and projecting monosynaptically to the output nuclei GPi and SNpr. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-05-07) — https://journals.physiology.org/doi/full/10.1152/jn.00527.2025 · keywords: Basal ganglia circuitry and dopamine neurobiology
- [statement] Rocha and colleagues describe indirect-pathway spiny projection neurons expressing Drd2 as projecting primarily to the GPe. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-05-07) — https://journals.physiology.org/doi/full/10.1152/jn.00527.2025 · keywords: Basal ganglia circuitry and dopamine neurobiology
- [statement] Rocha and colleagues state that activation of D1-like receptors stimulates the Gs-cAMP-PKA pathway and enhances neuronal excitability. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-05-07) — https://journals.physiology.org/doi/full/10.1152/jn.00527.2025 · keywords: Basal ganglia circuitry and dopamine neurobiology
- [statement] Rocha and colleagues state that D2-like receptor engagement recruits Gi proteins, reduces cAMP levels, and lowers excitability. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-05-07) — https://journals.physiology.org/doi/full/10.1152/jn.00527.2025 · keywords: Basal ganglia circuitry and dopamine neurobiology
- [statement] Rocha and colleagues describe the hyperdirect pathway as excitatory cerebral cortex projections to the STN that reinforce basal ganglia inhibitory output. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-05-07) — https://journals.physiology.org/doi/full/10.1152/jn.00527.2025 · keywords: Basal ganglia circuitry and dopamine neurobiology
- [statement] Rocha and colleagues describe basal ganglia output nuclei as influencing descending motor pathways as well as the thalamo-cortical pathway. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-05-07) — https://journals.physiology.org/doi/full/10.1152/jn.00527.2025 · keywords: Basal ganglia circuitry and dopamine neurobiology
- [statement] Cui and colleagues contrast the classical opposing-pathways model with their mouse observation of increased activity in both pathways at action initiation. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-05-07) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4039389/ · keywords: Basal ganglia circuitry and dopamine neurobiology · also: https://journals.physiology.org/doi/full/10.1152/jn.00527.2025
- [statement] Cui and colleagues used changes in GCAMP3 fluorescence intensity as a readout of neural activity, with lifetime and emission spectrum as controls for nonspecific fluorescence. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4039389/ · keywords: Basal ganglia circuitry and dopamine neurobiology
- [statement] The nigrostriatal axonal review states that the temporal sequence and causal relationship between early axonal functional abnormalities and structural degeneration remain unclear. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-13) — https://www.dovepress.com/degeneration-of-nigrostriatal-dopaminergic-axons-in-parkinsons-disease-peer-reviewed-fulltext-article-NDT · keywords: Basal ganglia circuitry and dopamine neurobiology
